title: Pip and Drift's Party Shell
markdown:
Pip was a busy, busy puffin. He waddled, waddled, waddled over the rocks, webbed feet going patter-patter. He loved smooth shiny pebbles for his cozy home. His eyes, bright as sea-glass, were always searching.

One blustery day a cheeky wind tumbled by. It ruffled his tidy feathers and — whoosh! — tried to snatch his favourite grey pebble from his beak. Pip held on. His heart went thump-thump-thump. He tucked the pebble deep into a crack in a big smooth rock and peeked, just to be sure it was snug.

A shimmering seashell bobbed near him. Not just any shell. It swirled with rainbow, like a bit of sunset caught and kept. Drift the dolphin had sent it. She was the gleamiest dolphin you ever did see, with a smile that could make a grumpy barnacle giggle. She nudged the shell with her nose.

“A party!” she chirped, voice like tiny bells underwater. “Under the sea! For everyone! We must deliver this before the moon is high. The Grand Coral Ball!”

Pip was a champion at puffin things: diving for fish, waddling with all his might. Drift was a whiz at dolphin things: leaping waves, singing to the currents. Delivering this invitation far and wide would be tricky. The sea was getting choppy. Waves leapt and splashed with extra energy.

Pip flapped, trying to lift above the swirl. Drift zipped, strong tail pushing them through. Faster and faster. Pip puffed his chest. Drift let out a soft puff from her blowhole.

Then a big grumpy cloud rolled in. Not just grey — gusty. It looked like a fuzzy elephant puffing its cheeks. It puffed, and whoosh! A huge wave crashed over Drift’s head. Splash! The shimmering shell tumbled from Pip’s beak, spinning in the spray.

Pip’s eyes went wide. Drift gave a little puff of surprise. “Oh dear!” Pip chirped, wobbling on a wave that felt like jelly. The pretty shell bobbed further away, lost in foam.

“We can’t out-speed this grumpy cloud!” Drift called, shaking water from her back.

Pip thought. He looked at his pebble, safe in its crack. He looked at the faraway shell. He looked at Drift, her happy smile a little sad.

“Together, Drift!” His voice grew stronger. “Not speed. We have to be smart.”

The cloud puffed again, a mighty whoosh that tried to shove the shell out to sea. Pip and Drift were ready. Pip, sturdy beak, hopped toward the bobbing prize and held it firm. Drift swam beside him, sleek body cutting a steadier path. When the wind pushed, Pip leaned into it like a tiny determined sail. When the waves tossed, Drift’s smooth side helped them glide. They used the wind’s own shove. A game of tag with the breeze, and the invitation was the prize.

Pip paused. He watched Drift glide. He felt the waves’ rhythm under his wobbly feet. They had to keep going.

The grumpy cloud, still grumbling, sent rain. Pitter-patter, pitter-patter. The sea grew more wobbly. The shell felt slippery. Pip gripped tighter. Drift’s happy leaps became steady strokes. The wind howled a little. Rain felt like tiny cold pebbles on feathers and skin. Little by little they went. Pip chirped. Drift flicked her tail.

Through the shimmering rain — a soft warm glow below the waves. Party lights!

They had made it. Not by being fastest. By being clever, together.

Pip nudged the shell onto a bright coral branch. Sparkly fish, shy seahorses, a giggling octopus — cheers.

A puffin and a dolphin had saved the party. Pip looked at the shell. It was more special than any pebble, because he had shared the journey. He still kept his grey pebble safe. He knew, now, that a shared adventure was a very good kind of treasure.

Patter-patter on the rocks, later. Whoosh in the memory. And a rainbow shell, delivered before the moon was high.
